result.title: MAPA: Mode-Aware Prototype Allocation for Latent Dataset Distillation in 3D Medical Classification
result.comment: Accepted at WACV 2027. 17 pages including supplementary material
result.summary: Dataset distillation (DD) synthesizes a small training set from a large one, but applying it to 3D medical classification is constrained by the memory and optimization costs of synthesizing full volumetric samples. Under a storage-equivalent budget, distilling in the latent space of a frozen autoencoder reduces this cost and fits more synthetic samples (prototypes) than in voxel space. However, class-level matching, such as distribution matching, causes prototypes to concentrate in dense latent regions while underrepresenting sparser intra-class regions, a consistent imbalance that we term prototype concentration. To address this, we propose MAPA (Mode-Aware Prototype Allocation), a latent distillation method that spreads prototypes across intra-class modes while preserving class-level matching. MAPA marks these modes with fixed anchors estimated by clustering the real latents and distributes prototypes over them through a soft assignment, together with a lightweight anti-collapse regularizer and curriculum weighting that stabilize the optimization. Across five 3D medical classification tasks, MAPA improves the aggregate balanced accuracy by +4.2 points over the strongest latent baseline while using the same number of prototypes. An exploratory severity analysis on MosMedData suggests improved worst-stratum recall without loss of normal-case specificity.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究在冻结自编码器的潜空间中做 3D 医学分类数据集蒸馏，提出 MAPA：用真实潜变量聚类得到的固定锚点标记类内模态，再以软分配将原型铺开到各模态，并配合轻量抗塌缩正则与课程加权稳定优化，缓解类级匹配造成的「原型集中」。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线无直接关系，但其潜空间中的模态覆盖与抗塌缩正则化线索，可供核查 latent 推理状态是否塌缩到主导潜区域、以及如何维持多种 latent 假设的多样性。
